Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 66, verse 1:

Naming of the surah

• It is called At-Tahrim (The Prohibition), because it mentions the Prophet's ﷺ prohibition upon himself of something that Allah had made lawful for him, and because it opens with a rebuke for that prohibition.

From the aims of the surah

• The cultivation of the Muslim household and the preparation of the most perfect model for a happy family, through the prohibition of divulging the secrets that exist between spouses; the warning to wives not to over-burden their husbands with annoyance; the exhortation to believers to educate and admonish their families and to work to protect them from the punishment of the Hereafter.

• The alerting of servants in general, and women in particular, to the fact that no one will avail another in the Hereafter, and that lineage and noble descent will not benefit a person if his deeds are not righteous; this is illustrated by two examples: an example of the disbelieving woman under the guardianship of a believer, and an example of the believing woman under the guardianship of a disbeliever.

[The Tafsir]

﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit yourself from what Allah has made lawful for you, seeking the pleasure of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful toward you.﴾

God has already prescribed for you, O believers, the dissolving of your oaths by paying expiation for them: feeding ten needy persons, or clothing them, or freeing a slave. Whoever cannot find [the means] then [must observe] a fast of three days. God is your Helper and the Guardian of your affairs; He is the All-Knowing of what sets your affairs right, so He prescribes it for you, and the All-Wise in His sayings and His deeds.

When the Prophet confided a matter to his wife Hafsah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she then told Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, and Allah informed him of her disclosure of his secret, he told Hafsah part of what she had reported, and turned away from informing her of the rest out of kindness. When he told her what she had disclosed of the conversation, she said: "Who told you this?" He said: "I was informed by Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Aware, from Whom nothing is hidden."

If you two (O Hafsa and Aisha) turn back to Allah in repentance, then indeed a matter that calls for repentance has already come from you both, for your hearts have leaned toward loving what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked, namely the divulging of his secret. But if you two band together against him with what would displease him, then indeed Allah is his protector and helper, and Jibril, and the righteous among the believers, and the angels after Allah's help are his aides and supporters against whoever harms him and shows enmity toward him.

It may be that his Lord, if he divorces you, O wives, will give him in place of you wives who are submissive to God in obedience, believing in God and His Messenger, obedient to God, returning to what God loves of obedience to Him, abundant in worship of Him, and fasting. Among them will be previously married women, and among them virgins.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted upon His law, protect yourselves by doing what Allah has commanded you and abandoning what He has forbidden you, and protect your families by what you protect yourselves with from a Fire whose fuel is men and stones. Over its inhabitants are angels, strong and harsh in their dealings, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and who carry out what they are commanded.

And it will be said to those who denied that Allah is the true God and disbelieved in Him, when they are cast into the Fire: "Do not offer excuses today. You are only being repaid for what you used to do in the world."

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law: turn back from your sins to obedience to Allah, a turning back after which there is no disobedience. It may be that your Lord will remove from you your bad deeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow, beneath their palaces and trees, on a Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him, nor punish them; rather, He will elevate their station. Their light will run before them and on their right hands as they walk upon the Sirat (the bridge over Hell), according to the measure of their deeds. They will say: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light, and forgive us; and pardon us our sins and cover them over for us. Indeed You are over all things Powerful."

O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites, and be stern with them. Their abode is Hell, and what an evil destination it is.

Wait, I need to translate faithfully and completely, not summarize. Here is the full translation:

O Prophet, strive against those who openly displayed disbelief and proclaimed it, and fight them with the sword; and strive against those who concealed disbelief and hid it, by means of proof (al-hujjah), the establishing of the prescribed punishments (al-hudud), and the rites of the religion (sha'a'ir al-din), and use harshness and severity with both groups in striving against them. Their dwelling-place to which they will return in the Hereafter is Hell, and wretched is that final destination to which they return.

The Noble Qur'an's Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 66, verse 10:

Allah sets forth an example for the state of the disbelievers, in their mixing with the Muslims, their closeness to them and their companionship with them, and that this does not benefit them because of their disbelief in Allah: the state of the wife of Allah's prophet Noah and the wife of Allah's prophet Lot. They were both under the marriage of two of Our righteous servants, but betrayal occurred from both of them towards them in religion, for they were both disbelievers. So these two messengers did not avail their wives anything against the punishment of Allah. It was said to the two wives: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter it." In setting forth this example is evidence that closeness to the prophets and the righteous benefits nothing when accompanied by evil deeds.

God has set forth an example for the believers—those who affirmed God, worshipped Him alone, and acted in accordance with His law—and that association with disbelievers in their dealings does not harm them—through the case of the wife of Pharaoh, who was married to the greatest of the disbelievers in God, while she herself was a believer in God, when she said: "My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise, and deliver me from Pharaoh and his mischief, and from the deeds of evil that proceed from him, and deliver me from the people who follow him in wrongdoing and misguidance, and from their punishment."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 66, verse 12:

God set forth an example for those who believe: Maryam daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity and preserved herself from fornication. So God commanded Jibreel (peace be upon him) to blow into the opening of her shirt, and the breath reached her womb, and she conceived Isa (peace be upon him). She affirmed the words of her Lord and acted upon His laws that He prescribed for His servants, and His books sent down upon His messengers, and she was among those who were obedient to Him.
